submitter: vigilant_designer_offer_analysis lane, bugs_open/395 fix candidate 1 (completion-time consumer for CLM-024)
rationale: bugs_open/395: `complete` means 'the handler reported success', and nothing on that path reads the item's own stated acceptance criterion. Since 2026-08-24 one producer writes a MACHINE-CHECKABLE half of that criterion into spec.acceptance_predicate (CLM-024), proven false of the page at emission. Nothing reads it. On its first live run the webdesign.co.uk index finding was dispatched to page-build-handler, which rebuilt and DEPLOYED the page (commit ee88ba3c, 2026-08-24 22:25Z) and closed the item `complete`; the page was rebuilt again on 2026-08-25; and its own stored predicate STILL REFUTES. This adds completion gate 1c beside the existing two: opt-in per item_type with the unsafe default OFF, three-valued so the zero value is not a policy, arming content_rewrite at RECORD-ONLY. Recording rather than refusing is the decision most open to challenge and the reason is stated: there is no live NEGATIVE CONTROL — all three live predicates refute, no row exists anywhere where a predicate is satisfied after its fix, and a gate that has only ever seen failures cannot be distinguished from one that refuses everything (395 section 6, which says this is not optional). Promotion to refusing is made a BUILD FAILURE unless the claim-timeout exclusion ships with it.

plan.summary: Completion gate 1c: re-evaluate an item's own machine-checkable acceptance predicate before stamping `complete`. Opt-in per item_type, three-valued outcome, content_rewrite armed at record-only.
plan.risks: THE LARGEST RISK IS A SILENT TOTAL FAILURE AND IT WAS FOUND WHILE BUILDING THIS, not reasoned about: a STORED predicate cannot be fed to EvaluateAcceptancePredicate. The evaluator enforces a closed key set per type and the emit side stamps verdict_at_emission / evidence_at_emission AFTER evaluating, so the stored shape carries two keys the evaluator refuses and a naive consumer gets `inapplicable` on 100% of live predicates — reading like a vocabulary problem in the model's output rather than a bug in the reader. Nothing caught it: the only test over real live predicates hand-writes them WITHOUT those keys, so it exercises a shape the database does not contain. Answered by single-sourcing the stamp and the strip (storedPredicate / predicateForEvaluation) and pinning them to each other with a round-trip test that fails when a THIRD provenance key is added. SECOND: the record-only arm is a third instance of CLM-023's residual — an enforcement arm proven by units and never fired in production. Mitigated three ways (the block arm is written and driven end-to-end through a fixture seam; the entry carries PromotionOwes stating its debt; promotion is a build failure without the claim-timeout exclusion) and NOT eliminated. THIRD: gate 1c adds one page-metadata SELECT per completion, but only for an armed type on an item that actually carries a predicate — 3 rows today. An unopted type does not reach the spec decode. FOURTH, a stated asymmetry with RFC_017: `inapplicable` records and never blocks. A stored predicate was evaluable at emission by construction, so unevaluable-now means the page left the surface, the vocabulary moved, or THIS GATE HAS GONE BLIND — and the third wears the same face as the other two, which is why it goes to agent_error_log as well as the row and blames the gate rather than the named page when the subject set is empty. Not blocking is only defensible while the outcome is record-only; a promoted type must revisit it. FIFTH: the claimed-item-timeout sweep writes site_work_items directly and NO completion gate runs for it. content_rewrite is not excluded. At record-only there is nothing to bypass; this is named as an open pre-existing hole rather than closed here.

CORRECTION TO THE FILED BUG: 395 section 4 says a verifier cannot do this because VerifyTarget carries the SPEC not the RESULT. That is gate 1b's argument and does not transfer — gate 1c needs the spec and the current page row, both of which a verifier has. The real reasons are that GetVerifier is one verifier per item_type on a type many producers file into, and that these gates compose

edits.rationale: Gate 1c. The decision points: the ROSTER LOOKUP IS THE FIRST STATEMENT, so an unopted type never reaches the spec decode, the DB read or a log line — byte-identical to today, which is what 'the unsafe default is OFF' has to mean. The outcome enum is three-valued for the same reason unreadableOutcome is (bugs_open/302): recording and refusing are unsafe in opposite directions and neither may be an author-time silent default. EVERY evaluated predicate leaves a verdict on the row INCLUDING `holds` — without that, a gate that permits is indistinguishable from a gate that never ran, which is exactly the residual the record-only entry carries. The roster lookup is indirected through a package var so a test can drive the refusing arm without mutating the map TestClaimTimeoutExclusionCoversBothCompletionGates reads (the verifierLookup precedent).

Single-source the emission stamp and its inverse, and let the page-surface query serve two callers. storedPredicate/predicateForEvaluation are defined together in the file that OWNS the stamping, so the writer and the reader cannot drift; widening acceptancePredicateFields to admit the provenance keys was the other option and is rejected — it would let a MODEL write its own verdict_at_emission and have the gate accept it, which is bugs_closed/335's self-attribution failure exactly. loadAcceptancePredicateSubjects takes *sql.DB instead of ActionParams (it used only params.DB) so the completion gate calls THE SAME function: the model authored against the page list it was shown, and evaluating over a different population would let a predicate be graded against a page that was not on the surface. One query, two ends of a predicate's life, no second WHERE clause to drift.

const (emissionVerdictKey = "verdict_at_emission"; emissionEvidenceKey = "evidence_at_emission")
var emissionProvenanceKeys = []string{emissionVerdictKey, emissionEvidenceKey}

func storedPredicate(pred map[string]interface{}, reason string) map[string]interface{}   // copy + stamp
func predicateForEvaluation(stored map[string]interface{}) map[string]interface{}         // copy - strip

-func loadAcceptancePredicateSubjects(ctx context.Context, params ActionParams, siteID uuid.UUID) (...)
-    rows, err := params.DB.QueryContext(ctx, `...`)
+func loadAcceptancePredicateSubjects(ctx context.Context, db *sql.DB, siteID uuid.UUID) (...)
+    rows, err := db.QueryContext(ctx, `...`)
  (call site: loadAcceptancePredicateSubjects(ctx, params.DB, siteID))

  emit side now: copied[acceptancePredicateKey] = storedPredicate(pred, reason)   // was 5 inline lines

edits.rationale: Wire gate 1c BETWEEN gate 1b and gate 2, and add the sixth blocked-completion cause. Placed before gate 2 because 1c grades the item's OWN stated criterion while gate 2 grades the TYPE's generic one — an item whose own terms are unmet should not be handed a generic `verified` that contradicts them. withAcceptancePredicate MERGES rather than replaces: an item can legitimately carry status='verified' AND a still-refuting predicate, and that pair IS bugs_open/395's finding, so flattening would destroy exactly the row that shows it. The fourth return value mirrors the existing abstention: recording needs ActionParams, which this function deliberately does not take.

Take the fourth return and record the blind spot, exactly as the caller already does for gate 1b's abstention — a pod log does not survive a roll. Also corrects a comment that is now load-bearing in the wrong direction: `verification != nil` has meant 'blocked' by coincidence until now, and since gate 1c a completion that PROCEEDS can carry a verdict too. Conflating the two would have made the permit arm invisible, which is the one arm proving the gate is not simply refusing everything.

Extend the lockstep contract to gate 1c, CONDITIONALLY on the entry's outcome — and this is the whole mechanism that stops the record-only arm becoming permanent by nobody remembering. Membership of acceptancePredicateGates does NOT imply the power to block (a recording entry lets completions through), so counting a recording entry would trip the REVERSE direction — an exclusion nothing can earn, the bugs_open/006 section C churn. Counting only REFUSING entries buys the thing no comment can: promoting an entry from predicateRecords to predicateRefuses is a BUILD FAILURE until the exclusion and its migration ship with it. Without it the promotion would arm a refusal the claimed-item-timeout sweep bypasses in silence, which is bugs_closed/317 again on a third gate.

The disconfirming tests. TestTheLiveStoredPredicateIsUnevaluableUntilStripped feeds the LIVE stored JSON verbatim (provenance keys and all) and asserts BOTH halves — `inapplicable` stored, `refutes` stripped — because either alone could pass for the wrong reason. The three controls are what make the refutation test evidence rather than a restatement: a satisfied predicate must PERMIT (the negative control, and it is labelled a UNIT and not a live row, because 395 section 6 asks for a live row and there is none); an unopted type must not even reach the page query (asserted by NOT queueing it in sqlmock, so the gate errors if it looks); an item with no predicate must record nothing. The refusing arm is driven through the lookup seam so it is proven to reach the caller. The roster test refuses an entry shipping without its declaration — including a record-only entry with no PromotionOwes.

edits.rationale: Declare ACCEPTANCE_PREDICATE_NOT_EVALUABLE in the same commit that writes it — caught by TestFindingCodeScanEveryWriteIsRegistered, which is the source-side early warning bugs_open/358 built. human-evidence, matching its sibling NO_CHANGE_GATE_UNREADABLE_RESULT one file along: no automated reader, and the `why` names the retention window it accepts. Its one interesting property is stated there — a stored predicate was evaluable at emission by construction, so a row means the page moved, the vocabulary moved, or the gate went blind, and the blind case re-fires on every completion so a 30-day window cannot hide it.
